statement: For every d ≥ 5, with the finite word set H defined above, the preceding construction produces a compact connected oriented smooth four-manifold M with nonempty boundary, a finite family F = (fr)r∈R of smooth proper disc maps with disjoint embedded boundary, and individually embedded framed sphere maps (gr)r∈R satisfying (2.7). If the circles ∂F bound pairwise disjoint proper locally flat embedded discs in M, the following data exist: (1) The compact oriented smooth four-manifold G has a homotopy equivalence p : G −→ Γ, where Γ is the rose on h0, h+, h−, q1, . . . , qd. The boundary is Q ∪ S e Ce, with the free group and peripheral coordinates of Lemma 2.1 and the longitude–meridian interchange (2.1). (2) There are disjoint cooriented smooth cuts J1, . . . , Jd, each a compact oriented three- manifold with one boundary torus and possibly additional closed components. Their boundary tori are the fixed product cuts in the Ce. (3) Cutting G along all Je gives a compact oriented smooth four-manifold X, possibly disconnected. With half collars absorbed into Q, its boundary is obtained by gluing Q to the two oppositely oriented copies of each Je along their boundary tori. Every torus-bearing wall component has just that one torus; closed wall components remain separate. Regluing the paired cuts recovers G. (4) The map on X lands in the graph cut open at the chosen qe points, namely Γh with the resulting half-edges; it is constant on every copy of a cut at its endpoint value. All words (2.3) are trivial in the fundamental group of the component XQ containing Q, with the original basings in Q. (5) Extend (2.8) to π1(Γ) by ρ(qe) = 1. The associated adjoint local system on G restricts to ρ on the h generators, to the identity on all za, and to a trivial system on each Je, with matching reference frames on its two copies induced by the graph point. The implication uses only the asserted embedded discs. It imposes neither output-dual conditions nor an additional framing or relative homotopy condition on those discs.
